title: DRV Book I  -  The Lock  -  REWRITE v2 (Phase 4.1 III)

canonical_node.axiom: The framework's formal system rests on three primitive axioms (God-as-Axiom, Trinity Isomorphism, Free Will) and a below-floor presupposition of Truth; the argument from properties of truth to the Logos is a derived chain, not a set of twenty independent axioms.
definitions: Truth: the below-floor presupposition that mathematical truths are necessary, eternal, universal, immaterial, coherent, discoverable, and existent (P0.1 - P0.7).
Logos: the name given to the ground of mathematical and moral truth (Definition 6.1).
God-as-Axiom (Axiom 1): the Logos is functionally identical to the terminal ground required by the von Neumann measurement chain, the regress argument, and the open-system requirement.
Central Claim: mathematical and moral truth share a single ground (Layer 5).
Master Equation: the operationalization of the Central Claim, with ten factors (including veracity, value, and alignment).
derivation: Layer 0: Truth exhibits seven properties (P0.1 - P0.7) as below-floor presuppositions.
Layer 1: Gdel-Chaitlin theorem (external) establishes that the ground of mathematical truth is external to mathematics.
Layer 2: From the theorem, the ground cannot be nothing, chaos, or deceptive (Inferences 2.1 - 2.3).
Layer 3: Source-Property Transmission Lemma transfers the seven properties plus veracity to the ground.
Layer 4: Definitions and postulates: truth is valuable, deception is wrong.
Layer 5: Central Claim: math and moral truth share a single ground.
Layer 6: The ground is named Logos and identified as Axiom 1 (God-as-Axiom).
canonical_node.action: The system should treat the three primitive axioms as the formal floor, treat the III argument as a derived chain with layer-specific epistemic status, and not push beyond the Feb 14 floor into divine mechanics.
boundary: Does not assert the seven properties as axioms; they are below-floor presuppositions.
Does not treat the Central Claim as an axiom; it is the thesis defended.
Does not exercise Axiom 2 (Trinity Isomorphism) in this series.
Does not descend below the Feb 14 floor (e.g., internal divine mechanics).
test: Check that each layer's epistemic status matches the taxonomy (below-floor, theorem, inference, lemma, definition, postulate, central claim, axiom).
Verify that the three primitive axioms are the only axioms used as load-bearing in the formal theory.
Confirm that the argument terminates at the Feb 14 floor and does not claim to prove divine internals.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Reclassifies the twenty axioms into a layered argument with distinct epistemic statuses, promoting A20 to the foundational Axiom 1 and demoting A1 - A7 to below-floor properties.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: The three primitive axioms (God-as-Axiom, Trinity Isomorphism, Free Will) remain the formal floor; the argument's content is preserved but reclassified.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the reclassification is removed, the framework reverts to a flat twenty-axiom structure that misrepresents the epistemic load and obscures the foundational role of Axiom 1.

overstatement_risks: Claims that the argument 'derives' the existence of the Logos, but the derivation relies on unproven postulates and a contestable moral inference.
Treats the Gdel-Chaitin theorem as forcing a specific metaphysical conclusion, which is an overreach.
The identity of indiscernibles argument for Axiom 1 assumes the profile is complete and unique.
kill_conditions: If the Gdel-Chaitin theorem does not entail an external ground, the argument collapses.
If the Source-Property Transmission Lemma is invalid, the transfer of properties fails.
If the Central Claim is not independently supported, the identification with the Logos is unsupported.
risk.lean_target: The document should be treated as a theological argument with a formal veneer, not as a mathematical proof. The reclassification is a structural improvement but does not establish the truth of the claims.

plain_summary: This document rewrites Section III of a theological work, reclassifying twenty axioms into a layered argument with distinct epistemic statuses. It promotes the final axiom to the foundational 'God-as-Axiom' and demotes the first seven to below-floor properties of truth. The rewrite is internally coherent but does not provide proof for its central claims; it remains a theological argument, not a formal proof.
